source_quality.text_layer: fluent prose; formula glyphs are lost, so every displayed equation was read from the page rasters

task_reconstruction: Widen the standing plan for the Great Lakes by treating them as a network whose flow takes time, then run two linear programs: one over the months that sets the reachable levels, and one over the hours of a day that hits them.

section_map.summary: summary: the network, the two nested algorithms and the two findings
introduction: the stakes, the seven stakeholders and the 2017 flood
the restatement and the case for linear programming
the two drawbacks of linear programs, then the assumptions
the dynamic network and the time expansion
the stakeholder preferences and the weighting
the constraint glosses and the reweighting rule
the lagged correlations and the two fitted lines
the extras, then the daily program
the sensitivity to the decay rate

contributions.summary: a time-expanded network that turns the delayed flow into an ordinary one
a long-horizon linear program whose only decisions are the two dam releases
a reweighting that hands the next period to the stakeholders the last one served worst
a daily program forced to end the day at the height the long schedule requires

dependency_graph.carries: the fitted flow lines and the lag times the level balance uses
the schedule each stakeholder's error is measured against
the height the lake must reach by the end of the day

assumptions.summary: the lake sizes stay constant, so flow converts to height at a fixed rate
the side channels are negligible next to the main outflows
the dams open or close within an hour and never fail
the flow is linear in the height over the small range observed

data_and_preprocessing.summary: the travel times, read off the peak of a lagged correlation
the two fitted lines, Niagara and Detroit, each with its coefficient of determination
the monthly rainfall, averaged over four decades and split into daily values

models.summary: the hydrosphere: two fitted lines and the lag times
the long program: four level balances, the safety bounds and the dam caps
the reweighting: the sixty-day error and the normalized shares
the daily program: the hourly balance and the end-of-day height

verification.summary: the schedules are run at three recorded rain levels and read by eye
both fitted lines carry a coefficient of determination
the decay rate is swept across a short range

results_trace.summary: managing the lowest lake means managing the highest one ahead of time
the lowest lake holds across the rain regimes while the highest swings
the model is sturdy against bad forecasts and touchy against wrong constants

writing_logic.summary: the summary names both algorithms, concedes the complexity and states two findings
the extra difficulty is justified and then reduced by a named method
the technique is praised before its two costs are conceded

language_observations.summary: importance is turned into a duty: because of the stake, it is in the best interest of the world
a departure is explained by one cause: the reason why our analysis differs is because water takes time
a choice is conceded at once: the link is admittedly tenuous
a limit is universalised and then redeemed: no model can completely avoid flooding, so predictable flooding is safe enough

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: a judge looking for advice to the body that runs the lakes gets a plan that keeps the standing scheme and says where it falls short
the memo is addressed to that body by name and tells it how the two dams would be run

weaknesses.summary: the flow penalty is weighted by one minus the sum of the stakeholder weights
Lake Erie's inflow is lagged while Lake Ontario's, in the next equation, is not
the reweighting has no cap and is never applied to printed errors
only two rivers get a printed line while the balance uses one for every lake
the error window is fixed at sixty days while the horizon is said to be the user's choice
the decay rate of 0.8 is used while the paper calls its evidence tenuous
one sentence says an adequate schedule is possible where the paragraph means none is
the rain comparison prints no error

independent_extensions.summary: the next period's weights set from each stakeholder's share of the last period's level error
